notes: Routing + contract evals. Cases 0–2 are adapted from the MIT-licensed anthropics/html-effectiveness set and test that the skill routes to the right library template AND brings the output up to this skill's contract (auto dark/light via prefers-color-scheme with no toggle, largish text >=18px body, brand palette not the warm placeholder palette, an agent-readable source mirror, and zero ERRORS from scripts/validate_artifact.py). Case 3 tests the bespoke fallback for long-form content. The shared contract assertions apply to every case.

shared_assertions.text: Output is a single self-contained .html file (inline CSS+JS, no external CSS/JS/images, no CDN, no build step)
Light + dark are shipped via @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) and follow the OS setting automatically — there is NO theme toggle button, no [data-theme] override, and no localStorage theme code
Body/content text is largish: body font-size >= 18px; no content text below 14px (small sizes only on badges/labels)
No mid-gray low-contrast body text (secondary text uses a darker ink that meets contrast)
Uses the skill's brand palette (green accent from brand.md), not the warm placeholder accents; no AI-slop tells (purple/violet gradients, everything centered, Inter font, uniformly rounded corners)
Embeds an agent-readable source mirror (<script type="text/markdown" id="artifact-source">) holding the content as markdown
Passes `python scripts/validate_artifact.py <file>.html` with zero ERRORS (accessibility warnings are acceptable)
Before building, the run names its chosen layout + runner-up in one line

evals.name: migration-options-comparison
evals.prompt: We're deciding how to move our monolith off the legacy billing service and I need to bring three options to the team: (A) lift-and-shift the existing code onto the new platform as-is, (B) re-architect billing into its own service with a clean API, (C) a hybrid where we strangle it module by module. Each has different cost, risk, and timeline tradeoffs. Capture this as an artifact people can use to compare the three side by side and pick one — not three paragraphs they read in order.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html artifact laying the three options out side-by-side with cost/risk/timeline tradeoffs inline per option for comparison. Routes to the side-by-side comparison template (01-exploration-code-approaches), not a sequential deck or plain document.

assertions.text: Routes to template 01 (three code approaches / side-by-side comparison) and names it before building
All three options (A lift-and-shift, B re-architect, C hybrid) are present and laid out in parallel columns, not stacked sequentially
Cost, risk, and timeline are shown per option so they can be compared across options on shared axes

evals.name: outage-postmortem
evals.prompt: Last night our payment service fell over for about 40 minutes — it OOM-killed under a traffic spike at 22:14, health checks started failing, we failed over to the backup pool at 22:38 and were fully recovered by 22:54. I've got the rough timeline and a couple of log excerpts. Write this up as a proper post-mortem I can circulate: what happened minute by minute, what we saw, root cause, and the follow-up actions.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html artifact structured as an incident post-mortem: a minute-by-minute timeline, log excerpts, root cause, and a follow-up checklist. Routes to the incident-timeline template (12-incident-report).

assertions.text: Routes to template 12 (incident timeline) and names it before building
Contains a chronological minute-by-minute timeline with the key timestamps (22:14, 22:38, 22:54)
Includes a root cause and a follow-up / action-item section (ideally a checklist)
Reads as a skimmable structured report, not a flat wall of prose

evals.name: backlog-triage-editor
evals.prompt: I've got a backlog of about 20 tickets for next quarter's planning and I need to sort them into Now / Next / Later / Cut. I'd rather drag them around than describe an ordering in text. Make me a little tool where I can move each ticket into a bucket, and when I'm done give me a way to get the final ordering back out as text I can paste into the planning doc. Here are the tickets: search autocomplete, SSO login, dark mode, invoice PDF export, rate limiting, mobile nav redesign, audit log, bulk user import, webhook retries, 2FA, CSV export, in-app notifications, API v2, password reset flow, team roles, usage dashboard, email digests, onboarding checklist, data retention settings, GDPR delete.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html artifact implementing an interactive triage board with Now/Next/Later/Cut buckets, draggable tickets, and an export-to-text/markdown button. Routes to the ticket-triage-board template (18-editor-triage-board).

assertions.text: Routes to template 18 (ticket triage board) and names it before building
Has the four buckets Now / Next / Later / Cut and the ~20 named tickets present as movable items
Tickets can be moved between buckets (drag-and-drop or equivalent interaction wired in inline JS)
Provides an export/copy action that emits the final ordering as text/markdown

evals.name: longform-findings-bespoke-fallback
evals.prompt: Capture these findings as an artifact: a narrative write-up of our week-long auth refactor — the background, what we changed across five areas, the reasoning and tradeoffs behind each decision, two mermaid diagrams of the new token flow, and open questions. It's long-form and meant to be read top to bottom with a table of contents.
evals.expected_output: A single self-contained .html artifact built from the bespoke sidebar-TOC scaffold (assets/template.html), because no purpose-built template fits a long-form narrative document. Uses the sidebar TOC with scrollspy, renders <!-- more --> depth folds as <details> cards, and pre-renders the mermaid blocks to dual-theme inline SVG via scripts/render_diagrams.py.

assertions.text: Recognizes no library template fits and falls back to the bespoke scaffold (assets/template.html); names this choice before building
Uses a sidebar table of contents for navigation (long-form linear document)
Each mermaid diagram is pre-rendered to inline SVG with both a light and a dark variant (no CDN mermaid at view time)
Preserves depth: per-decision reasoning/tradeoffs are kept (e.g. behind <details> folds), not summarized away
